title: KL divergence as a log-likelihood-ratio sum (absolutely continuous case)
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite measurable space, and let $\mu$ and $
u$ be finite measures on $\Omega$ with $\mu$ absolutely continuous with respect to $
u$. Write $	frac{d\mu}{d
u}$ for the Radon–Nikodym derivative and let $\mathrm{llr}(\omega) = \log 	frac{d\mu}{d
u}(\omega)$ be the log-likelihood ratio at $\omega$. Then the Kullback–Leibler divergence satisfies
\[
  D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu \,\|\, 
u)
  = \left[\; \sum_{\omega \in \Omega} \mu(\{\omega\})\,\mathrm{llr}(\omega) \;+\; 
u(\Omega) \;-\; \mu(\Omega) \;ight]_{+},
\]
where $[\,x\,]_{+}$ denotes the value in $[0,\infty]$ obtained by viewing the real number $x$ as a nonnegative extended real, negative values being sent to $0$.
hypotheses_covered: Ω is a finite measurable space (finite and discrete)
μ and ν are finite measures on Ω
μ is absolutely continuous with respect to ν
replaced:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite measurable space and let $\mu, \nu$ be finite measures on $\Omega$
with $\mu \ll \nu$.  Then
\[
  D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu \,\|\, \nu)
  = \mathrm{ofReal}\!\left(
      \sum_{\omega : \Omega} \mu.\mathrm{real}\,\{\omega\} \cdot \mathrm{llr}(\mu,\nu,\omega)
      + \nu.\mathrm{real}\,\mathrm{univ}
      - \mu.\mathrm{real}\,\mathrm{univ}
    \right),
\]
where $\mathrm{llr}(\mu,\nu,\omega) = \log \frac{d\mu}{d\nu}(\omega)$ is the
log-likelihood ratio at $\omega$.
